slides.texte_overlay:
How to become ridiculously
social in your 20s
Host a monthly dinner. Same day every month, different guests each time. Mixing friends from work, sport and school builds a social circle that grows by itself.
Learn a social sport. Padel, five-a-side, volleyball. Team sports give you a group, a reason to meet every week, and drinks after the game where friendships form.
Introduce people to each other. "You two have to meet, you both love climbing." Connecting others makes you the centre of a network without even trying.
Always bring a good story. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having something surprising to share makes me easy to talk to anywhere.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Having something surprising to share makes me easy to talk to anywhere.

slides.texte_overlay: Say hello to your neighbours. A name, a smile, a short chat in the hallway. Knowing the people around you turns your street into a small community of your own.
Travel with friends at least once a year. Even a weekend away. Shared trips create inside jokes and memories that keep a group close and laughing for years.
Make the first move with new people. Most people are waiting for someone else to start. "Hey, I'm Tom, first time here?" is all it takes to make a new friend.
